items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Horace Henderson in his oral history interview said that Benny used to call Fletcher... Did you know about any of that, or did that happen to you? [INTERVIEWEE] No.

ctx.x: She lived on 138th Street and Lenox Avenue somewhere. Don't go there alone now, especially if you're white. But in those days they didn't do anything.
Horace Henderson in his oral history interview said that Benny used to call Fletcher in the middle of the night and tell him, will you please do such and such a chart, I need it for a recording
session the next day, or something like that. Did you know about any of that, or did that happen to you?

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: And I tell you another great trumpet player and great arranger that was in that band, and I know you know him, Eddie Sauter.

ctx.x: I heard him about two years ago. He's been with the Jazz Party at Dick Gibson's.

Well, he was in that Charlie Barnett Band, and there was a great pianist in that band named Bill Miller, and I think he's out to MGM now. Man, he could play. He was a quiet little guy, and he could write. Oh, man, he could write like mad. And he had a trumpet player named Bernie Priven. I think it's P-r-i-v-e-n, I think; man, he could play. And he had a first trumpet player, a little short guy named Spots Esposito, we called him, you know.
And I tell you another great trumpet player and great arranger that was in that band, and I know you know him, Eddie Sauter.
